title: Minimum eating speed
statement: Piles of bananas piles; each hour you eat up to k bananas from one pile (a pile smaller than k still takes the whole hour). Return the minimum integer k that finishes everything within h hours (h ≥ number of piles).
hints: If speed k works, does k + 1 work?
Binary search k over [1, max pile] with the test sum(ceil(p / k)) ≤ h.

solution.explanation: The answer space is monotone: if k finishes in time, any larger k does too. So binary-search the smallest feasible k with the lower-bound template; each test costs O(n). This "guess the answer, check feasibility" move solves a whole family of optimisation problems.
solution.python:
def min_eating_speed(piles, h):
    lo, hi = 1, max(piles)
    while lo < hi:
        k = (lo + hi) // 2
        if sum((p + k - 1) // k for p in piles) <= h: hi = k
        else: lo = k + 1
    return lo
